glossary.Deep vein: A large vein running deep in the muscles, as opposed to the superficial veins under the skin.
glossary.Venous obstruction: A blockage to blood flowing back through a vein.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A clot that has travelled to and blocked an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Long-haul travel: A long flight or journey, usually over 4 hours, causing prolonged sitting.
glossary.Immobility: Not moving about, e.g. bed-bound after illness or surgery.
glossary.Oestrogen: A female sex hormone in the pill and HRT that makes blood clot more easily.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, usually a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.Erythema: Redness of the skin from increased blood flow.
glossary.Pleuritic chest pain: Sharp chest pain that is worse on breathing in.
glossary.Tachycardia: A fast heart rate, over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Hypoxia: Low oxygen levels in the blood or tissues.
glossary.Doppler: Ultrasound that measures blood flow, used to see if a vein is blocked.
glossary.Interim anticoagulation: Starting a blood thinner while waiting for a scan to confirm or exclude a clot.
glossary.Cast immobilisation: A limb held still in a plaster cast, a risk factor for DVT.
glossary.Collateral veins: Extra veins that open up to carry blood around a blockage.
glossary.Palpation: Examining by feeling with the hands.
glossary.Cancer-associated thrombosis: A blood clot caused by an active cancer making the blood clot more easily.
glossary.Prophylaxis: Treatment given to prevent a disease rather than treat it.
glossary.Prophylactic-dose: A lower dose given to prevent clots rather than treat one.
glossary.Venous stasis: Slow or pooled blood flow in the veins.
glossary.Endothelial injury: Damage to the inner lining of a blood vessel.
glossary.Hypercoagulability: An increased tendency of the blood to clot.
glossary.Valve pockets: Small spaces behind vein valves where blood flows slowly and clots start.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factor reactions that ends with thrombin making a fibrin clot.
glossary.Thrombus: A blood clot formed inside a vessel.
glossary.Propagate: To grow and extend along the vessel.
glossary.Proximally: Towards the centre of the body, e.g. from calf up to thigh.
glossary.Pulmonary arteries: The arteries carrying blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
glossary.Factor X: A clotting factor that, once activated to Xa, converts prothrombin to thrombin.
glossary.Fibrin: The protein mesh that forms the structure of a blood clot.
glossary.Venous hypertension: Persistently high pressure in the leg veins.
glossary.Valve incompetence: Vein valves that no longer close, letting blood flow backwards.
glossary.Vitamin K: A vitamin the liver needs to make clotting factors; warfarin blocks its action.
